the agent claims an offer and reports the end of the job. Agents call the first four; users call the rest.

Take the offer for a task. The task starts (in_progress) and the agent may then ask for the job token.

Running and pending jobs in one flat list, with the reason a pending job waits.
The latest scheduler events, newest first.

Stop a worker taking new jobs (drain: true) or let it take them again (drain: false). Its running jobs finish. Admins only.
The usage of a worker's machine, or of a task's job, over the last minutes (default 60).

datachunks._description: Object storage for artifacts, datasets, models and debug data. The client asks for a presigned URL with its task token, uploads the bytes straight to the store, then commits. Downloads use presigned URLs too.

2.8.description: Record a pending upload and return a presigned PUT URL for its bytes. The caller must have write access to the task, or hold a job token for it. The headers returned must be sent with the PUT. Size and sha256 are bound to the URL.
A presigned PUT for one part of a multipart upload. The response headers must be sent with the part. Each part's ETag is returned by S3 and goes into commit.

Check the stored object against the record (size and sha256). A mismatch deletes the object. A multipart upload is completed from its parts first. Only the upload's own task may commit a job's upload.
Return a presigned GET URL for a stored object, by datachunk id, or by task, kind and name (the newest stored object with that name). Only stored objects can be downloaded.
Remove stored objects and their records, by datachunk id, or by task, kind and name. Callers need write access to the task (or hold its job token).

Exchange a short assertion signed with the device's key for a short-lived access token.
List devices: the caller's own, or all devices for an admin.
Revoke a device. Its next request is refused. Allowed for the owner and for an admin.
An agent asks for a token to run one task it has taken. The token acts as the task's owner, for that task only, and ends with the job.
A read-only token for one task's GitHub repository, for the job or the agent running it. The token is valid for about an hour and can read only that repository.
